title: Terminal stream: one SSE for every terminal, with replay or snap on join
what:
GET /hub/term/events?since=t1:4096,t3:0. The first frame is term-list.
Joining:
- A terminal named in `since` whose seq is still inside the ring resumes as term-out from that seq.
- Any other terminal gets term-reset {id, seq, data, snap}. data is the whole ring when the ring still starts at byte 0 (exact replay). Otherwise snap.rs synthesizes it from alacritty:
  - RIS
  - DECSET for the modes the Term holds: ?1 DECCKM, keypad, ?2004, ?1000/1002/1003/1006, ?1004, ?1049, ?25, DECSTBM
  - the visible grid with SGR runs
  - the cursor
Frames:
- term-out {id, seq, data b64}, term-size, term-title {id, title, fg}
- term-input {id, by:'agent', chat, text ≤ 200 chars, control chars shown as ⏎ ^C ⇥}
- term-exit {id, code, signal}, term-closed, term-hold, term-open
- hub-stream-end {reason: stopping}
Every frame has a string type (sse.js:36). Frames are coalesced per 16 ms, at most 32 KiB raw each, with a ':' keep-alive every 15 s.
The Body is hand-written like proxy.rs's Proxied (no new futures dep) and ends when ctx.stop fires, so it never eats RESPONSE_DRAIN.
Each client keeps its own cursor; a client that falls behind the ring start gets term-reset.
Exports Terms::note_input(id, by, chat, text) for T2.
tests:
tests/term_stream.rs:
- replay from a given seq
- with a 4 KiB ring (--knob term_ring=4096): after the shell sets DECCKM and prints past the ring, term-reset has snap:true and contains the DECCKM set
- a terminal under the ring size gets an exact replay
- perch SIGTERM ends the stream and the process exits in under 3 s
- every frame parses with a string type
- a keep-alive is seen (knob shortens the interval)
live_check: fake perch on PORT=48114: `curl -N` the stream while posting input.
risk: The snap is our own VT encoder. A wrong one gives a bad repaint, never code execution. Test the modes TUIs use (vim, htop, less).
